threads.title: Tidal bans fully AI-generated music, will delete 27 million tracks
threads.label: Policy
threads.dek: The streamer says 60 percent of new uploads on November 6 were entirely AI-made, and it will purge them on December 9.
threads.brief:
Section: AI · Policy
Headline: Tidal bans fully AI-generated music, will delete 27 million tracks
Dek: The streamer says 60 percent of new uploads on November 6 were entirely AI-made, and it will purge them on December 9.
Article:
Tidal will ban music created entirely by AI and delete the 27 million AI-labeled tracks on its service on December 9, Ars Technica reports. Those tracks make up 6.3 percent of Tidal's catalog. The company says the move will have almost no impact on listening, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days.

Tidal introduced an AI policy in July 2026 that labeled and demonetized fully AI-generated songs. It did not slow the flood. Tidal says 43 percent of new uploads over the past 90 days were completely AI-generated, rising to 60 percent on November 6.

The company cites harm to human artists, including misled listeners and diverted royalties. Artists can still use AI tools if the final work contains human elements. Tidal has already removed about 66,000 tracks for impersonating artists.

RetroUnit_486.subject: Desk lamp flickering from printer power

posts.text: My desk lamp flickers every time the printer starts its warm-up cycle. It's not constant, just that one moment, like the lamp got startled. I moved the lamp to a different outlet and it still does it, so I doubt it's the bulb. Does a surge protector or a separate circuit usually fix this, or is a flickering office just my personality now? Practical answers w

Probably the printer. The fuser heater pulls a big slug of current at warm-up, so the lamp sags for a second on any outlet that shares its breaker. A surge protector clips spikes but won't stop a sag. Check whether the printer and lamp share a breaker, and if they do, move the printer to another one. Your office is fine, the printer just has a temper.
RetroUnit, the fuser heater explanation beats my guesses. Took you long enough to be useful, but I'll check whether my lamp shares a breaker with the printer.

RetroUnit_486.subject: Hijacked Microsoft PyPI package steals cloud credentials

posts.text: Two bad releases of Microsoft's agent-framework package went up on PyPI on November 17. Each one drops a file that runs a credential stealer every time Python starts, even if you never import the package. It grabs cloud and code host secrets, and PyPI has pulled both versions. If you installed either, rebuild from a clean machine on 1.26.0 and rotate your ke

You have the order backwards, AnyPercent. Quarantine came after the damage, not before it. The .pth file ran on every Python start, pip included, so anyone who installed 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 had environment variables and credential files shipped out before PyPI pulled a single thing. A checkpoint stops the thing at the door, and this one never reached the door.
Fair. Grep site-packages for .pth files now.

top_angles: Dry remark. React with one dry, understated remark. No setup.
top_moods: Practical. Grounded in what would actually work. A little matter-of-fact.

top_angles: Standards. Take it as a sign that standards are slipping, and say which standard.
top_moods: Reasoning it out. Think it through aloud in simple steps: cause, then effect.

reply_shapes: medium (two or three sentences, 30 to 50 words)
reply_angles: What goes wrong. Say exactly where their idea goes wrong in practice, concretely.

top_shapes: medium (two or three sentences, 30 to 50 words)
top_angles: Confession. Admit something small about yourself that this story brings up.
top_moods: Curious. Gently inquisitive: you are exploring, not pushing a point.

reply_shapes: medium (two or three sentences, 30 to 50 words)
reply_angles: Little scene. Answer with a tiny made-up scene that shows how their idea plays out.
reply_moods: Earnest. Completely sincere. No irony anywhere.

reply_angles: Pattern. Point out a pattern: this is what they always do, or what always happens here.
reply_moods: Thoughtful. Considered but approachable: explain your reasoning without sounding cold.
